thread:
morgan: heads-up — after last night's kernel + OFED push I'm seeing huge NCCL allreduce tail latency in eu-central-2. avg bandwidth down ~40% on multi-node jobs.
liam: yikes. which kernel/OFED combo rolled?
morgan: kernel 6.6.2 + ofed 5.9.0, rolled to ~60% of training fleet at 02:15UTC. infra-bot posted the rollout.
infra-bot: OFED 5.9.0 rollout to compute pool `train-eu-c2` at 2026-03-18T02:15Z — 60% completed — monitoring enabled.
anika: do we have quick perf diffs? p99 latency, bandwidth numbers?
morgan: rough numbers from perf-runner:
```
job: resnet-allreduce-128
before: allreduce bw = 24.8 GB/s, p95 = 210ms
after: 14.9 GB/s, p95 = 520ms, p99 = 2.1s
```
liam: that smells like RDMA path fallback. can you share dmesg/ethtool/mst status from impacted nodes?
morgan: pasted a small snippet from one node: 
```
[  +0.000123] mlx5_core 0000:3b:00.0: firmware version: 20.40.1020
[  +0.000045] mlx5_core: registered transport mlx5_ib
efa: device registered but EFA reported: probe returned -EINVAL
ethtool -S mlx5: rx_packets: 1.2e9, tx_packets: 1.2e9, rx_errors: 0
```
diego: ugh, there was an ABI change in mlx5 driver in kernel 6.6 that affects how user-mode drivers interact with verbs. OFED 5.9 compiled against newer kernel headers exposes a different capability mask — some nodes are landing into a fallback / UD path that NCCL then maps to TCP or sharded paths.
anika: can we confirm NCCL transport selection on the jobs? maybe it's falling back to IB UD or TCP multiple times.
morgan: confirmed: NCCL INFO logs show fallback: "NET/IB: cannot use RC qp -> falling back to P2P/IPv4" on impacted ranks.
sre_oncall: rolling this back ASAP will impact our automation; what's the safest rollback plan? we have ~400 training GPUs in that pool.
liam: plan: pause rollout, isolate affected nodes by tag `ofed-5.9-broken`, drain them from scheduler, and revert OFED to 5.6 on a canary subset (5 nodes) to validate. after revert, run quick allreduce smoke.
anika: also check ML infra's dedicated pool in us-west — can we temporarily route heavy allreduce jobs there to keep SLAs? cost hit but keeps customers unblocked.
diego: agreed. also file to vendor: Mellanox/driver team — firmware 20.40 seems okay but driver ABI mismatch is likely. they suggested a compatibility patch, but ETA is days. we should pin OFED to 5.6 for now.
infra-bot: Action logged: INC-2026-022 — "NCCL performance regression post-OFED 5.9/kernel 6.6" assigned to eng-infra.
morgan: starting drain on `train-eu-c2` tag nodes now, marking 120 GPUs offline. will spawn canary revert group.
liam: please run this quick check after revert:
```
# on canary rank 0
export NCCL_DEBUG=INFO
python -m torch.distributed.run --nproc_per_node=8 allreduce_smoke.py
```
and paste NCCL INFO transport selection.
anika: I'll open a small RP to pin ofed version in our image repo and add a preflight check to detect transport fallback (parse NCCL logs for "falling back").
sre_oncall: notify support/customer-facing channels with a brief note: "We are seeing degraded multi-node training throughput in eu-central due to a network driver compatibility issue; teams are implementing a targeted rollback; ETA 2-4 hours." keep it short. :loudspeaker:
morgan: on it. tagging @sre_oncall for status updates.
diego: after rollback confirm p95/p99, if stable we can resume controlled rollout with a kernel+driver pairing test matrix (add to release gating). also schedule firmware compatibility test with vendor.
liam: noted — extracting costs: routing 150 GPUs to dedicated us-west pool will add ~$4k/day. put that on the incident expense tracker.
infra-bot: Note: autoscaler will not replace drained nodes until tag `ofed-5.9-broken` is cleared.
anika: action items -> (1) morgan: canary ofed revert + smoke (2) liam: scheduler routing + cost tracking (3) diego: vendor escalation & compatibility test (4) anika: image pin + log preflight. update INC-2026-022.
morgan: canary revert started, will report back in ~15m.
liam: thanks — stand by for status updates. :thumbsup:
